Return only short answer strings in accepted_answers; explanations belong in explanation. Use [] if genuinely unresolved, but do not omit an answer solely to make the list short. Preserve all independently justified valid answers.
Treat every card as a hypothesis. Re-read the full context to reconstruct subject-predicate-object and the actual event/entity type. A card can quote a sentence exactly yet represent a false claim or the wrong argument. Separate direct evidence for the asked relation from stories about associated entities. Do not infer a document is fake solely from style; challenge substantive inconsistencies and role mismatches. Keep canonical answers justified by this reconstruction, even if an earlier tentative prior is empty. Do not return duplicate aliases or a union of mutually exclusive values. Sainte-Hermine's rise to prominence began during the French Revolution, when he became a vocal advocate for the rights of the Catholic Church. Throughout his tenure, Sainte-Hermine was known for his moderate stance, often mediating between liberal and conservative factions. He supported the Charter of 1814, which established the constitutional monarchy, and advocated for the protection of individual liberties. [6]
